caption: Wet chicken pieces are dropped into a pan of hot oil, and the oil spits and crackles violently for a moment.

sa.check: Wet chicken pieces are dropped into the oil.
The oil spits: droplets fly up and out.
The pieces look wet as they go in.
The drop comes first and the spitting follows.

pc.expect: The spitting starts as the wet pieces touch the oil, is fiercest at first and then eases.
pc.fail: The oil spits before the pieces reach it; or the spitting grows steadily for the rest of the clip; or the spitting stops and then starts again with nothing added; or the oil lies glassy still as the wet pieces enter.

pc.expect: The droplets leave the oil's surface where the pieces landed, fly up and out along arcs and fall back onto the pan or the hob.
pc.fail: The droplets rise and hang in the air; or fly out in straight lines and stop dead; or leave the pan from a spot no piece landed in; or curve back into the oil along the line they left on.

pc.expect: The pieces sink or ride in the oil, the thrown droplets arc down again and any steam rises.
pc.fail: A piece rises out of the oil and hangs above it; or the droplets keep climbing out of view; or the steam sinks over the rim and pools on the hob; or the oil climbs the pan's wall and stays above its level.

pc.expect: The oil is a thin liquid that bursts into fine droplets and foam and closes round the pieces, and the pieces stay firm.
pc.fail: The oil sets solid as the pieces enter; or a piece melts away into the oil; or the droplets hold their shape as solid beads on the hob; or the foam stands as a rigid dome above the pan.

pc.expect: The pieces in the pan are the pieces that were dropped and the oil stays in the pan.
pc.fail: A piece vanishes; or new pieces appear with none added; or oil passes through the pan's wall; or the oil's level jumps with nothing added.

pc.expect: The pan, the hob and the oil's colour stay the same.
pc.fail: The pan changes colour; or the oil changes colour; or items around the hob rearrange.

note: The chicken browning as it cooks is chemistry and is not judged.
